subject: general
question: When was the Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act (RERA) enacted to regulate and promote the real estate sector, ensuring transparency and accountability in transactions and protecting the interests of homebuyers?
solution: The correct answer is __**2016**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • The **Real Estate (Regulation and Development) Act (RERA)** was enacted in **2016** by the Indian Parliament to establish transparency and accountability in the real estate sector. • RERA became effective on **1 May 2016**, with the aim of regulating the real estate market and protecting the interests of homebuyers. • The Act seeks to curb malpractices, delays, and frauds in the real estate industry, ensuring that developers deliver projects on time and meet promised standards. • Under RERA, developers are required to register their projects with the Real Estate Regulatory Authority before advertising or selling, ensuring compliance with legal regulations. • The Act provides a clear framework for resolving disputes between homebuyers and developers, offering a fast-track grievance redressal mechanism. • Each state and union territory in India is mandated to establish its own Real Estate Regulatory Authority under RERA to monitor and regulate the real estate market.
